entries.en: Controls if damage numbers should appear above enemies when they take damage.

'Hey, what's up pal, I'm trying to get to Death as well you see. I'm not following you or those other two idiots if that's what you're thinking. Just felt like going to the beach, getting some sun.
You know what, I've been here a long time, maybe I could give you some tips on how to cross the Desert!'

entries.en:
'Hello, 

I hope you are well. I am writing to you regarding the upcoming deadline on your fight with Death. I am attaching my guidance on how to cross the desert.
If you have any questions, please let me know, but do NOT ask any third parties such as incompetent wizards or idiotic rogues!

Best regards, Your Only Attorney in this Wretched Place, 
Sign Here: .........'

The warrior sounds absurd, but you could use some help around here.

entries.en:
Before you rise the ancient judgemental stones, silent sentinels of the Moor, their surfaces etched with mystic runes.
Cold and unmoving, they pulse with a faint, eerie glow, their eyes - carved deep into the stone - watching all who approach. Standing in the center you focus your mind and prepare to take their trial. What do you your strengths lie?

You extend your hand towards the rune at the top and suddenly your ears catch a whirr as it cracks and in a flash of light it forms a link, connecting you to its wellspring of arcane force.

You place your hand on the core inscription and gradually sense the stone's energy passing through you, your thoughts alone guiding its flow.

entries.en: Your curiosity gets the best of you and you knock on the door. With a creaking sound it opens, and an even more bizarre sight unfolds as you see a mouse, a rabbit, a fox, a wolf and a bear, sharing what seems to be a much larger space on the inside than what's on the outside. The creatures greet you kindly, inviting you to join them and tell you of their stories. As if time wasn't passing inside, you spend a while in there... but whose stories did you take to heart the most?

entries.en: The damaged glass probes, the messy counter, the pieces of paper scattered everywhere, the brass instruments… The lab of a scientist who has been studying Darkmoor. There is so much to explore here and the mystery of the man or creature that has created and abandoned this place peaks your curioisity. But there is not enough time to get the the bottom of this and all you need to do is decide how to make use of your finding.

entries.en: The Treefolk's eyes glow up and his branches rustle as you approach. 'Mmyees... it is you…' - he murmurs as his sight slowly focuses on you - 'Whispers of your quest have reached me through this Moor’s decrepid trees… I would love nothing more than to help you smash, whack, crush and burn the foul creatures corrupting this land.' Upon a waive of his hand the Treefolk's ancient magic surges through you…

entries.en:
Countless moons I spent building my legacy, myriad sacrifices made. Yet, in a mere moment, all was undone - a wooden stake, wielded by that perfidious professor.

But in despair’s heart, an obscure path was revealed. An offer from Death himself, which I embraced. Soon, Helsing will join these timeless realms, and it will be I who shall savor the last, resonating mirth.

entries.en:
By Death’s decree, I am now Baron of the Outer Circle. Whilst some may deem this title lesser than my former status as Count, I embrace it as a new chapter of rebirth. Indeed, my powers here grow with a fervor unknown before.

Still, the burden of deeds remains. I ponder seeking Death's counsel on the matter of my own conscription.

entries.en:
A conundrum. To Death, I made my plea for the privilege to recruit mine own vassal and it has been met with an ample proposition. Alas, it entails the repossession of Van Helsing's soul unto the urns. I surmise 'twas Mort that persuaded him to impose this condition. She seems to possess a peculiar leniency towards mortals.

Perchance, mine own thirst for vengeance hath been quenched enough. One can only hope that this Necromancer proves a worthy trade for such a sacrifice.

entries.en:
The Lady of the Lake, her tenure here far outspans my own. Her powers, subtle and pervasive, infuse this land. Even the blades of grass under my dominion carry her signature scent.

Enamored am I, my former wives now distant echoes. Alas, in this liaison, it seems the scales of power are tipped in her favor.

entries.en:
The bond with the Lady of the Lake hath dissolved. Though eternity be vast, the sting of this rupture lingers. She hath spurned and forsaken me.

My thoughts now turn to companions of a different sort. These gargoyles of which I've heard, they shall serve me well. Indeed, I stand in need of added strength to safeguard my dominion.

entries.en:
In Death's domain, where silence reigns,
I build my shrines to break its chains.
With melody and rhythm's might,
my music shrines can bring the light.

Each note a brick, each song a stone,
In halls of shadow, I'm not alone.
For in these shrines, the music plays,
A beacon bright in endless greys.

entries.en:
Top of the necromancy game while alive, and now I get an offer from the Grim Reaper himself? Peak career move. But now I'm reporting to a vampire. Just my luck. 

Even in the afterlife, you can't dodge the corporate ladder. Still, if you've got to work under someone, might as well be the undead elite.

entries.en:
Raising the dead? That's my kind of party trick. This place, though, it's a necromancer's dream - endless supplies, endless possibilities. I'm like a kid in a mortuary. Sadly, research and development is always shelved for the mundane task of skeleton assembly... 

P.S. I got it! I will build a construct that can summon skeletons autonomously! Now that's efficiency at the workplace!

entries.en:
Eureka!
The ‘Summoners’ are alive! Well, as alive as they need to be. To make one requires a ton of bones and more chants than monastery monks. Yet, once complete, they're a one-entity skeleton factory. At last, I finally have more time for my research!

Note to self: Prototype a Summoner for Summoners? The potential for automation is immense.

entries.en:
Research is a joy with more time at hand! That being said, I've hit a roadblock with my latest project.

The goal: a formidable undead knight, fully encased in metal armor. It still needs a skeleton underneath, as bones are the scaffolding for my spells. And herein lies the problem - the enchantments are simply not powerful enough to move that massive armor… 

One does not simply put a ton of metal on an undead skeleton, it seems.

entries.en:
My black knights are now complete, thanks to two breakthroughs!

Firstly, I struck gold with a dusty alchemy book. It described an ancient cohesion elixir that I used to fill the space between bone and metal, greatly magnifying my enchantments!

The second breakthrough is entirely of my own. Bubbles! I am still not sure why exactly, but carbonating the formula has almost doubled its effectiveness! A big POP in the joint field of Necromancy and Alchemy!

The second breakthrough is entirely of my own. Bubbles! I am still not sure why exactly, but carbonating the formula has almost doubled its effectiveness! A big POP in the joint field of Necromancy and Alchemy!

entries.en:
Necromancy is dead, pun intended. I'm writing a new chapter here. Sure, creating bone puppets is great and all, but I just changed the whole game.

I managed to infuse an actual soul back into the bones! These guys aren't just stronger – they've got the smarts!

Though, on second thought, giving bones a brain might just backfire…

entries.en:
'First Bloom'

To the Lady, whose silence commandeth more than words may,

I have long moved as the world demanded, swift and unrelenting. But thou, thou remainest - as though the world itself must shift to honour thy stillness.

Thou walk’st the quiet places with the grace of moonlight through stained glass. What art is thine, that thou dost quell the bloodlust in me, not with chains nor charms, but with mere presence?

Perhaps it is not magic, but truth - plain and unspoken. Or perhaps it is thee, simply thee.
I find myself drawn. And in that, I find… peace.

If such a thing is truly mine to know.
~ Dracula

entries.en:
'The Lilly'

To the Lady, whose nearness hath become as breath to me,

Thy presence hath not waned since first I beheld thee - in truth, it grows. Like a root winding softly through stone, thou hast found thy way through the hollows of my being.

I think often of that eve by the pale fen, where we sat with naught between us but fog and time. Thou didst pluck a lily, half-wilted, and set it upon my chest. I asked if 'twas a token, and thou said simply: 'All things bloom again.' I heard thy meaning then - but I feel it more now.

With thee, I find myself not Count, nor Baron - only thine.
~ Vlad

entries.en:
'The Crown Left Untaken'

To the Lady, whose silence once brought solace,

I had thought, perchance, the time was right.

When I placed the circlet in thy hands - no iron, nor gold, but woven of willow and blood-vine - I did not speak of titles, nor chains, nor rule. Only closeness. Only us. 

Thou didst not cast it away, yet neither didst thou wear it. Thy fingers closed soft upon it, as if it were a bird one dare not wake. Then turned thy gaze to the water, and said nothing more. I do not know what that silence meant.

It is thy nature, I know, to drift. To bloom, but not bind. I have loved that in thee. I still do. Yet now I wonder - am I to be part of thy stillness, or merely one who watches from the shore?

I speak not in anger. Only in ache.
If I have erred, forgive me. I sought not to claim thee, but to offer something shared.

I remain, ever at the water’s edge - waiting.
~ Vlad

Then he decided to start protecting the mortals too - from avalanches, snowstorms... all of Winter's ‘gifts’. So the people started celebrating in his name.

But then he really overdid it with the ‘free stuff’ business. It's like he's mocking my trade! 
Heh, the ‘holiday spirit’. Two can play at that game.

To show that I'm an imp of heart too, here's a tab on me!

entries.en: Despite their eery appearance, Mimicbags are shy and cautious creatures. Lightweight as a feather, they will carry all of your gear for you and become a most loyal and trusty companion - provided you have earned their trust. It is even said that in time they grow to like and mimic their companion's appearance.
